statement_record.book: A functor U : D → C is MONADIC if it has a left adjoint F ⊣ U such that the comparison functor Φ : D → C^T for the induced monad T = UF is an equivalence of categories; the forgetful functors from algebraic categories (monoids, groups, rings) to Sets are the typical examples, and monadicity may be taken as the definition of 'algebraic'.

[given A : F ⊣ U and A' : F' ⊣ U'.  Instantiating F := L, U := U, F' := U, U' := R at an adjoint triple L ⊣ U ⊣ R yields exactly (U ◯ L) ⊣ (U ◯ R), i.e. T ⊣ G]
Theorem Adjunction_Monad : F ⊣ U → @Monad D (U ◯ F).  [at the left leg L ⊣ U this is the monad T = U ◯ L on C]
Definition Adjunction_Comonad (A : F ⊣ U) : @Comonad C (F ◯ U).  [at the right leg U ⊣ R this is the comonad G = U ◯ R on C]

statement_record.book: Given three composable adjoint functors L ⊣ U ⊣ R with L, R : C → D and U : D → C, one obtains simultaneously a monad T = U∘L and a comonad G = U∘R on C, and moreover T ⊣ G. Instantiated by colim ⊣ Δ ⊣ lim, giving the comonad Δ∘lim and the monad Δ∘colim on a diagram category.
statement_record.intree: Adjunction_Compose : (F' ◯ F) ⊣ (U ◯ U') for any composable pair of adjunctions; Adjunction_Monad : F ⊣ U → @Monad D (U ◯ F); Adjunction_Comonad (A : F ⊣ U) : @Comonad C (F ◯ U).
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-stronger on the three general clauses (each is proved for arbitrary adjunctions, and the adjoint triple is a type-checking instantiation with no extra hypotheses: Adjunction_Compose applied to L ⊣ U and U ⊣ R is literally (U ◯ L) ⊣ (U ◯ R)); intree-weaker on the instantiation clause, which cannot even be stated.
